title: Enterprise Offline Diagnostic Bundle and Customer Handback Protocol
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary:
Provide a standardized, privacy-conscious process for producing an "offline diagnostic bundle" (ODB) that support engineers assemble and hand back to enterprise customers for offline analysis. This document codifies when and how to generate an ODB, required artifacts, redaction and sampling rules, packaging format, delivery SLA, and verification steps. The ODB is intended only for allowed support/legal/engineering stakeholders and must follow the redaction rules and retention constraints below.

Audience:
- Customer Success Engineers (CSEs)
- Solutions Engineers (SEs)
- Support oncall and L2/L3 engineers
- Customer security/compliance reviewers

When to use this runbook:
1) Customer requests an offline bundle for root-cause analysis after an escalated incident (SEV1/SEV2) or quality investigation that cannot be resolved with live telemetry.
2) Legal or compliance requires an extract for audit that cannot be satisfied by live telemetry exports.
3) Customer asks for a reproducible data slice for model-eval or labeling that must be processed offline.

Primary objectives:
- Provide engineers with a deterministic, reproducible bundle sufficient for debugging (trace IDs, request payloads, timestamps, small model artifacts) while minimizing PII/exposure.
- Meet customer compliance requirements (data minimization, pseudonymization) and Redwood's internal confidentiality controls.
- Deliver within a clear SLA and with traceable ownership.

Ownership and approvals:
- Requesting party: CSE assigned to the account (owns request, notifications, customer signoff).
- Producer: Support engineer (L2+).
- Approver: Security reviewer (required when bundle contains <confidential> data fields or when customer is in regulated industry).
- Delivery: Secure transfer by CSE (S3 pre-signed URL with expiration, or SFTP endpoint approved by customer).

Delivery SLA (target):
- High (SEV1 / legal): 24 hours initial package + 48 hours full package.
- Medium (SEV2 / QBR request): 72 hours.
- Low (non-urgent request): 10 business days.

Required artifacts (minimum):
- manifest.yaml (see spec below)
- request-sample.jsonl (sampled inference requests, max 10k rows by default)
- response-sample.jsonl (associated model responses)
- traces/ (zipped set of trace files matching sample request IDs)
- ingress-metadata.csv (tenant id, route, model name, client-ip-hash)
- runtime-metrics.csv (CPU/GPU utilization and latency histograms for the window)
- config-snapshot.json (model routing, quantization profile, batch config at time-of-incident)
- optional: small model checkpoint diff (<=100MB) OR model-profiles.txt (performance/kv cache stats)

Manifest spec (manifest.yaml) - example fields:
- bundle_id: string (UUID)
- tenant_id: string (pseudonymized)
- time_window_start: RFC3339 timestamp
- time_window_end: RFC3339 timestamp
- request_count: integer
- sample_strategy: deterministic | random | criteria-filtered
- redaction_profile_version: v1.3
- produced_by: <engineer name/email>
- verification_hash: sha256 hex of the top-level tarball

Packaging format and file layout (tar.gz):
- bundle-<bundle_id>.tar.gz
  - manifest.yaml
  - samples/request-sample.jsonl
  - samples/response-sample.jsonl
  - traces/traces-<bundle_id>.zip
  - metadata/ingress-metadata.csv
  - metadata/runtime-metrics.csv
  - config/config-snapshot.json
  - redaction-log.txt
  - verification/sha256.txt

Sanitization and redaction rules (MUST follow):
1) PII removal: Remove or pseudonymize any fields defined in Redwoods PII catalog. Common examples: user_email, user_name, phone_number, ssn, credit_card_number. Replace with deterministic pseudonym hash: sha256(<tenant_salt>+<original_value>) truncated to 16 chars.
2) IP handling: Replace client_ip with hashed_ip = sha256(client_ip + tenant_salt) and remove last-octet for IPv4 if hashing is not permitted.
3) Sensitive customer tokens/keys: redact entirely (REDACTED) and record the key name in redaction-log.txt.
4) Full-text heuristics: For response payloads, scan with the redaction regex list (Appendix A). If heuristics match >3 tokens resembling PII, remove full utterance and record in redaction-log.txt.
5) Audit trail: Every automated redaction must append a single-line entry to redaction-log.txt with fields: file,path,redaction_type,rule_id,timestamp,operator.

Sampling policy (defaults and overrides):
- Default sampling: stratified by route and latency bucket — choose up to 1% of total requests or 10k rows (whichever smaller), with deterministic seeding (tenant_id + time_window_start).
- For model-quality investigations: allow up to 50k rows if customer approves and security reviewer signs off.
- For legal/audit: follow the exact custody instructions from legal; do not exceed requested scope.

Step-by-step production procedure (numbered):
1) Intake and verify authorization
   a) CSE confirms written customer authorization including allowed data categories and transfer mechanism.
   b) If customer is in regulated sector (finance/health/government), require security approval before extraction.
2) Create an incident branch and set bundle_id: uuidgen
3) Reserve temporary storage: create ephemeral S3 prefix named s3://redwood-sandbox/odb/<bundle_id>/ with 7-day lifecycle.
4) Run extraction script (example CLI below) with redaction_profile=v1.3 and deterministic seed.
5) Validate manifest.yaml and run redaction audit tool (must produce zero high-severity violations).
6) Compute verification hash and sign with producer's GPG key (optional internal requirement).
7) Move tar.gz to secure delivery area and populate pre-signed URL with 72-hour expiry (unless customer requires shorter).
8) Notify customer and internal stakeholders with delivery checklist and access instructions.
9) After handback confirmation, schedule automated deletion per retention policy.

Example CLI and commands (reference):
# create bundle (internal tool: odb-create)
# requires: --start, --end, --tenant, --profile, --seed
$ odb-create --tenant tenant-1234 --start 2026-02-01T08:00:00Z --end 2026-02-01T12:00:00Z --profile v1.3 --seed 20260201T08 --out /tmp/odb-<bundle_id>.tar.gz

# validate redaction audit (internal tool: odb-verify)
$ odb-verify /tmp/odb-<bundle_id>.tar.gz --policy redaction-v1.3 --report /tmp/verify-report-<bundle_id>.json

# compute sha256 (verify)
$ sha256sum /tmp/odb-<bundle_id>.tar.gz > verification/sha256.txt

Delivery checklist (must include):
- Customer authorization record attached to support ticket (ticket ID)
- Security approval if required
- manifest.yaml verified and signed by producer
- redaction-log.txt present and non-empty
- verification/sha256.txt matches transmitted archive
- Delivery mechanism documented (S3 pre-signed URL expiry, recipient email, audit entries)

Retention and deletion policy:
- Default retention: 7 days from bundle creation.
- Extended retention: up to 90 days only with documented customer approval and security signoff.
- After retention window, support automation will run secure-delete (s3 rm + immutable-delete for external storage) and append deletion record to ticket.

Verification and customer acceptance:
- After delivery, CSE requests customer confirmation that the bundle meets their needs and whether additional slices are required.
- If customer requests further slices, repeat intake and follow the sampling/approval steps.

Troubleshooting common failure modes:
- "Extraction exceeded storage quota": switch to filtered extraction (shorter window) and request quota bump from eng-infra with priority label.
- "Redaction audit failed": escalate to security reviewer, provide failure report, and hold delivery until reviewed.
- "Customer rejects bundle for missing context": work with the customer to identify missing IDs or specific trace ranges, re-run extraction with narrow time window.

Appendix A: Example redaction regex list (non-exhaustive)
- email: [A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}
- ssn (US): \\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\\b
- credit card: (?:4[0-9]{12}(?:[0-9]{3})?|5[1-5][0-9]{14}|3[47][0-9]{13})

Appendix B: Example manifest.yaml (minimal)
bundle_id: "123e4567-e89b-12d3-a456-426614174000"
tenant_id: "tenant-xxxx"
time_window_start: "2026-02-01T08:00:00Z"
time_window_end: "2026-02-01T12:00:00Z"
sample_strategy: "deterministic"
redaction_profile_version: "v1.3"
request_count: "87432"
produced_by: "mchen@redwood.ai"

Appendix C: FAQ (short)
Q: Customer wants the raw client IPs for forensic analysis.
A: Do NOT provide raw IPs unless customer signs a justified exceptional data access form and security approves. Prefer hashed_ip with tenant_salt.

Q: Can we provide full model checkpoints?
A: Only provide model artifacts under an approved data transfer agreement and never include customer data embedded in the checkpoint. Prefer model diffs and profiling text files.
